page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-12 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine utilizing the x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs and 45.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory allocation of 3.75 GB per core. The instance is equipped with a single NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU, provisioned as a fractional one-quarter GPU resource to support hardware-accelerated workloads.

This server configuration does not include local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the fractional GPU allocation allows organizations to access dedicated graphics acceleration capabilities without the financial overhead of provisioning a full, undivided physical GPU.

The g4-standard-12 is designed for workloads requiring moderate GPU acceleration combined with multi-core CPU processing. Suitable applications include entry-level 3D rendering, remote workstation hosting, computer-aided design, and low-intensity machine learning inference tasks.
